LESSON: HAND TOOLS AND EQUIPMENT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: WOODWORK
Strand: Foundations of Woodworking
Topic 1.3: Hand Tools and equipment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 26

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Hand Tools and equipment, part of Foundations of Woodworking in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 WOODWORK.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to use hand tools correctly? 2. Why is it important to care for and maintain hand tools in a Wood workshop?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify different types of hand tools and equipment in the workshop,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Hand Tools and equipment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. classify different hand tools in the wood workshop,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Hand Tools and equipment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. demonstrate safe use of hand tools and equipment in wood workshop,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Hand Tools and equipment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. care and maintain hand tools during and after use in wood workshop,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Hand Tools and equipment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the importance of using the correct hand tools and equipment for a given task.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Hand Tools and equipment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

A. identify different types of hand tools and equipment in the workshop,

C. demonstrate safe use of hand tools and equipment in wood workshop,

   Hand Tools and equipment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. care and maintain hand tools during and after use in wood workshop,

   Hand Tools and equipment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate the importance of using the correct hand tools and equipment for a given task.

   Hand Tools and equipment helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use visual aids to identify hand tools used in wood workshop
2. categorise the classes of woodworking hand tools; measuring, marking out, cutting, sharpening, boring, planing, impelling, holding/clamping, tools shaping.Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by peers or they could write or use assistive technology to communicate their responses.
3. sketch and label different types of hand tools, learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of their body to sketch and 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Hand Tools and equipment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: learner develops speaking, listening and teamwork skills when brainstorming

different types of equipment used in the workshop

● Critical thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops evaluation and decision making skills when drawing and

labelling different types of hand tools.

● Digital literacy: learner develops digital skills when interacting and manipulating digital devices to identify hand tools

used in wood workshops.

Values:
● Responsibility: Learner cares for tools and equipment as they practice safe use.

● Unity: learner cooperates with others when watching video clips and discussing uses of hand tools.

● Integrity: learner apply laid down procedure when practicing safe use of hand tools and equipment

● Peace: learner avoid hurting others when practicing safe use of hand tools and equipment

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Safety and security: learners observe safety for self when working with tools.

● Social cohesion : learner discuss in groups how to care and maintain hand tools and equipment

Suggested learning resources: adapted hand tools such as cutting tools, sharpening tools, measuring and marking tools,

planning tools, adapted basic safety equipment, realia, adapted drawing materials.
